findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`, relying on Prisma to implicitly bump `@updatedAt`; Prisma throws `PrismaClientValidationError` ("Argument `data` must not be empty") for empty-data `updateMany` unless the client's `@updatedAt` special-case applies, and this sits on the availability-fetch path where a throw would break calendar sync — make the touch explicit (`data: { updatedAt: new Date() }`) or verify behavior against the pinned Prisma version

[Medium/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 — `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the current working directory, not the script location; invoked from the repo root (`bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) it reads/edits — and via `touch` may create — a `.env` outside the repository, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never written to the real env file; use a script-relative path (`"$(dirname "$0")/../.env"`)

[Medium/test_gap] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts — no tests were added for the new mutation, in particular the ownership check (that a user cannot delete cache rows for a credential they don't own) and the successful deletion path
[Low/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:66 — `sed -i '' -E "s|..."` is BSD/macOS-only syntax; GNU sed (Linux) treats `''` as the script and fails, so the env-file update errors out on Linux machines

[Low/api] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:24 — throws a plain `Error` instead of a `TRPCError` with a proper code (e.g., `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`); tRPC converts it to a 500 "unexpected error", misclassifying an expected authorization failure (noisy for error tracking) and the descriptive message never reaches the client

[Low/performance] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27 — instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly, so the `CalendarCache` groupBy runs on every `connectedCalendars` request even when the calendar-cache feature is disabled; the PR extends `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` (whose purpose is the disabled path) with `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` but the production caller never uses that selection — gate on the feature flag like other consumers

[Low/bug] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:85 — `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` hardcodes the locale, so the "Last updated" timestamp renders in US-English format for all users in a fully i18n'd app; derive the locale from `useLocale()`/`i18n.language`

[Low/bug] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:41 — `deleteCacheMutation` doesn't invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` itself (unlike `disconnectMutation`, which invalidates in `onSettled`); the refreshed `cacheUpdatedAt` depends entirely on the optional `onSuccess` prop, so without it the dropdown keeps showing the stale "Last updated" time after a successful delete

[Low/bug] apps/web/package.json:11 — `dev:cron` switched to `npx tsx`, which bypasses the workspace lockfile and may download an unpinned tsx at runtime (non-deterministic, network-dependent); declare `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it via the package manager instead

[Low/test_gap] packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173 — `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (and the `cacheUpdatedAt` enrichment in `connectedCalendars.handler`) have no test coverage; the mock implementation added for the new method is never exercised

goldens.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5 — `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the current working directory, not the script location; invoked from the repo root (`bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) it reads/edits — and via `touch` may create — a `.env` outside the repository, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never written to the real env file; use a script-relative path (`"$(dirname "$0")/../.env"`)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, `ENV_FILE` is set to a relative path (`ENV_FILE="../.env"`). Relative paths in shell scripts resolve from the caller’s current working directory, not the script directory. If run as suggested from the repo root (`bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), this points to `../.env` (outside the repo) and the script may `touch`/edit the wrong file, so `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` won’t be written to the intended repo `.env`. Using a script-relative path via `$(dirname "$0")` would fix this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `deleteCache` TRPC mutation and handler (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx`, `deleteCache.handler.ts`) with nontrivial logic: it checks credential ownership via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` and then deletes rows via `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })`. No corresponding test changes/additions are shown anywhere in the diff to cover (a) access denial when the credential is not owned by the session user and (b) the successful deletion path. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a functional defect in the code shown.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the handler now does `const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();` and immediately calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, which performs a Prisma `calendarCache.groupBy(...)`. The diff also extends `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` with the same method and logs that it’s used when “calendar-cache [is] disabled”, but this caller never chooses the mock/disabled path because it hard-codes the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository`. That makes the extra DB query run on every `connectedCalendars` request and bypasses any feature-flag/DI-based repository selection that the mock implies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:41 — `deleteCacheMutation` doesn't invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` itself (unlike `disconnectMutation`, which invalidates in `onSettled`); the refreshed `cacheUpdatedAt` depends entirely on the optional `onSuccess` prop, so without it the dropdown keeps showing the stale "Last updated" time after a successful delete

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess?.()`; it does not invalidate any TRPC queries (unlike `disconnectMutation`, which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`). Since `cacheUpdatedAt` is passed in as a prop and the list data is populated via `connectedCalendarsHandler` (which derives `cacheUpdatedAt` from DB), the UI will only refresh if the parent triggers a refetch via `onSuccess`. In this diff’s current usages (`SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`), `onSuccess={onChanged}` is provided, so it’s not a guaranteed broken behavior here, but the component is reusable and can easily show stale cache timestamps if `onSuccess` isn’t wired.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/package.json:11 — `dev:cron` switched to `npx tsx`, which bypasses the workspace lockfile and may download an unpinned tsx at runtime (non-deterministic, network-dependent); declare `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it via the package manager instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the `dev:cron` script from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` in `apps/web/package.json`. Using `npx` can execute a package that is not installed in the workspace (fetching it on-demand), which makes the script potentially non-deterministic and network-dependent unless `tsx` is ensured as a project dependency. The diff does not show `tsx` being added as a devDependency here, so the reviewer concern is a valid tooling/reproducibility issue but not an application correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173 — `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (and the `cacheUpdatedAt` enrichment in `connectedCalendars.handler`) have no test coverage; the mock implementation added for the new method is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial logic (`CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` using Prisma `groupBy` and the `cacheUpdatedAt` enrichment in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`) plus a corresponding mock method, but this PR diff shows no added/updated tests exercising either path. While the repo may have existing coverage elsewhere, nothing in the diff demonstrates tests were added for these new behaviors.
